html:
Baden was a German state on the east bank of the upper Rhine, facing France, including much of the Black Forest. It is on the map from 1715 to 1815, growing in the last snapshots.

Its margraves, a branch of the Zähringen family, ruled from the 1100s. In 1535 the land split between two lines, Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach, and suffered badly in the wars with France. In 1715 the margrave of Baden-Durlach founded Karlsruhe, a new capital with streets fanning out from the palace. The two halves were reunited in 1771.

Napoleon made Baden much larger. It became an electorate in 1803 and a grand duchy in 1806, as a member of his Confederation of the Rhine. Its constitution of 1818 was one of the most liberal in Germany, and it was a centre of the revolutions of 1848. Baden joined the German Empire in 1871. The monarchy ended in 1918, and in 1952 Baden merged with Württemberg in the modern state of Germany.
